seatsSat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard

confirmed.problem: The card's move menu is positioned with the inline style `left:8px;top:-250px` — a constant — at every card, in every lane, at 390, 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920, with a fine pointer and with a coarse one. I measured the rect as [8,−250,188,213] in all twelve combinations I drove. The menu is entirely above the top of the viewport and never visible. The cause is at src/tasks.js:2041: `const host = window.__SUITE.host("tasks")` returns DIV.app, which the suite shell sets to `display: contents`, so `host.getBoundingClientRect()` is all zeros; `top = Math.min(box.bottom - frame.top + 6, frame.height - 250)` therefore always picks `0 - 250`. The menu's actual offset parent is `.floor`, not the host, so the origin is wrong twice over. Meanwhile `.menuVeil` renders at the full viewport size and is transparent, so the board looks untouched and the person's next click is eaten dismissing an invisible menu.
confirmed.consequence: Orla presses the only control on a card labelled "Move this task" and absolutely nothing happens on screen — twice, because the veil swallows her second press too. On her phone this is not one route of three: drag is a pointer gesture she cannot make and Space-carry needs a keyboard, so the source's own comment calls this menu "the one route to moving a card that a mouse, a finger and a keyboard can all take". On a phone the board's primary action is unreachable. Keyboard focus does enter the menu, so a screen-reader user operates a control nobody can see.
confirmed.fix: In the `menu` branch of src/tasks.js (~2038–2046) stop measuring the suite host. Take the origin from the menu's real offset parent and the clamp from the viewport: `const frame = document.querySelector('.floor').getBoundingClientRect(); let top = box.bottom - frame.top + 6; let left = Math.min(box.left - frame.left, innerWidth - frame.left - 200); if (box.bottom + 219 > innerHeight) top = box.top - frame.top - 219;` then `menuAt = 'left:' + Math.max(8, Math.round(left)) + 'px;top:' + Math.round(top) + 'px'`. Never clamp against a rect that can be zero — a `display: contents` ancestor must not be able to decide where a popover lands.
confirmed.assertion: For every lane's first card, at 390×844 (touch), 768×1024, 1280×900, 1440×960 and 1920×1000: open the menu from `.cardDots`, then assert `.cardMenu`'s rect is fully inside the viewport (top ≥ 0, bottom ≤ innerHeight, left ≥ 0, right ≤ innerWidth), that `document.elementFromPoint` at its centre is inside `.cardMenu`, and that the rect for a card low in a lane differs from the rect for a card at the top of that lane.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, and every number in it is exact. Driven in Chromium against file:///C:/.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board at 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x900, 1440x960 and 1920x1000, with a fine pointer and with a coarse/touch context, clicking .cardDots on the first, middle and last card in each: the style attribute is literally `left:8px;top:-250px` and the rect is [8,-250,188,213] in all of them. The menu's bottom edge is at -37; it is entirely above the viewport at every card, in every lane, at every width.

The diagnosis is right down to the element. `window.__SUITE.host("tasks")` is `hostOf()` in src/app.js:86-88, which returns `[data-app="tasks"]`, i.e. DIV.app, and src/shell.css:93 sets `.app { display: contents; }`. I measured `host.getBoundingClientRect()` at runtime: [0,0,0,0] at all five widths. So at src/tasks.js:2044-2045 `top = Math.min(box.bottom - 0 + 6, 0 - 250)` always resolves to -250 and `left = Math.min(box.left, -200)` is floored to 8 by the Math.max. The seat is also right that the origin is wrong twice over: I read `menu.offsetParent` and it is DIV.floor, never the host.

The consequences are as described. `.menuVeil` measures [0,0,390,844] / [0,0,1440,960] with `background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0)`, and `document.elementFromPoint(centre)` returns DIV.menuVeil — the board looks untouched and the next click is eaten. Focus lands on BUTTON "To do" inside the invisible menu (`document.activeElement.textContent === "To do"`), so a mouse user is now typing into something 250px above the window. The aria-live region is empty, so nothing is announced either.

Blocking is the correct class, not overstated. The code's own comment at src/tasks.css:891-892 and src/tasks.js:800-802 says this menu is "the one route to moving a card that a mouse, a finger and a keyboard can all take… on a touch screen there was no way at all to move a card" — and at ≤720 src/tasks.css:1465 makes .cardDots permanently visible, so on Orla's phone this is the only advertised way to move a card and it does nothing visible. The product does not do what it says.

Not a restatement of either gate: I grepped interaction-check.mjs for cardMenu / cardDots / menuVeil / moveto and there is not one assertion. It cannot be — `cardMenu()` returns "" unless `menuFor` is set, and no gated state sets it, so the menu is not in the DOM in any shot or any checked state. This is precisely what automation cannot see. Not in the 34 already-fixed list, not in the refuted list, not a lessons.md class.

I also verified the proposed fix's premises rather than taking them on trust, because the fix hardcodes `.floor`: there is exactly one `.floor` in _gate-suite.html, _gate-tasks.html AND master.html (so tasks.js does not throw when run standalone); its computed border is 0px on all sides, so its border box and padding box share an origin and getBoundingClientRect is the right rect for an absolutely-positioned child; `position: relative`, `overflow: visible`, scrollTop/scrollLeft 0 with scrollHeight === clientHeight, so no scroll offset to correct for; and no ancestor of the host carries a transform, filter, perspective or paint containment. The fix's own geometry checks out: I replayed its formula against every .cardDots box at all five widths and every menu that corresponds to an actually-clickable card lands fully inside the viewport. The only "failures" in the replay are cards that are themselves off-screen (below the tray fold at 390, or in a lane scrolled off to the right at box.left 1469), which you cannot click without first scrolling them in.

So: correct problem, correct diagnosis, correct severity, and a fix whose direction and origin are verified sound. It is confirmed. Two numbers in it are soft rather than wrong, and it is missing two clamps — sharpened below.

REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — do not discard the observation, and do not ship this remedy.

THE PROBLEM REPRODUCES, ALMOST EXACTLY. Driven in chromium at 1920x1000 against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, clicking `.rail [data-rail]` in turn with no reload:
- sheet 100..1902 (1802) in all three — correct.
- wordmark ink: tasks 128, notes 311, timeline 140 — correct.
- head trailing cluster right: `.headActions` tasks 1874, notes 1691 — correct, 183px apart.

Timeline's wordmark sits 12px inboard of the other two at EVERY width, and on a different band (top 58 vs 37/38). The head's trailing cluster ends up floating with ~390px of white to its right on a sheet whose other two products park theirs 28px from the edge.
- `.pile` (the desk paper) **does not move**: still 311..1691, while `.index` is now 100..1540. The two stacked planes visibly disagree on both edges. That is precisely the defect notes.css:139-155 records as already found and fixed once — "at 1920 the two objects the architecture calls stacked planes shared neither edge ... the two planes agreeing is the architecture." The fix reopens a closed defect in the locked direction (Notes · Direction C, The Stack).
- The parenthetical "(and the desk's flex container) change align-items: center to flex-start" cannot be applied: `.desk` (notes.css:305) is a row flex with `justify-content: center` and no `align-items` declaration at all. The tasks.css doctrine quoted at :383 is real and I verified it, but it is about a GRID whose columns overflow the scroller — `justify-content: safe start` exists so leading cards stay reachable. Notes' stack does not overflow anything. The doctrine does not transfer to "left-anchor a centred column and leave its sibling plane centred."

SEVERITY, corrected: defect, not blocking or misleading. Nothing fails to work and nothing untrue is asserted; a person switching products sees the wordmark jump 183px at one declared viewport. Visibly wrong, passable.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (chromium, 390x844, hasTouch, isMobile, deviceScaleFactor 2, against _gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=…):
- tasks.board and tasks.dense: suite-tile centres 50 / 118 / 186 / 254, .railAdd 317, .railAvatar 357. Verbatim.
- timeline.owner-flight and timeline.phone: 56.8 / 138.3 / 219.8 / 301.3, .railAdd display:none, .railAvatar 357. Verbatim.
- Deltas 6.8 / 20.3 / 33.8 / 47.3. Verbatim.
- Insets: rail spans x 9–381; first tile x 28 → 19px leading vs avatar right 373 → 8px trailing in Tasks; 34.8 → 25.8 vs 8 in Timeline. Verbatim.
- And the part the seat only implied, which I drove and which is the real severity: press the Timeline tile in Tasks at 232–276; after the switch that same tile occupies 279.3–323.3. Overlap = 0px. The tile you pressed is entirely out from under the thumb — the shift (47.3) exceeds the tile (44). That is a genuine phone-level defect, not taste.

WHERE THE DIAGNOSIS IS LOOSE: it names `.rail`'s `space-around` as the redistributor. `.rail`'s space-around distributes nothing, because `.railGroup { flex: 1 }` absorbs all free space at ≤720. The freed 54px (44 add + 8 + 2 margins) goes entirely into `.railGroup`, whose OWN `justify-content: space-around` spreads the four tiles: group width 270 in Tasks, 324 in Timeline. Same outcome, wrong level — and the fix is aimed at the wrong level as a result.

WHY THE FIX FAILS:
1. The four tiles are ALREADY wrapped in a leading cluster. `.railGroup` exists (line 7888) and already carries `display:flex` at ≤720. "Wrap them" is half-shipped; what is missing is only `flex` and `justify-content`.
2. The stated origins are wrong by 11px on all four. Rail padding is `0 8px`, so a leading cluster flush to the content edge starts at 9+8 = 17.
3. The fix's two promises cannot both hold. x = 28 means a 19px leading inset against an 8px trailing one — exactly the asymmetry it claims to remove "as a side effect". Equalised insets require 17 and 8/8. The finding asks for both.
4. The inert spacer is dead weight. I built it (44px + the 8/2 margins, in the trailing cluster, before the avatar) and compared against no spacer: the avatar lands at 341–373 in Timeline either way, because `margin-inline-start:auto` already pins the trailing pair to the padding edge. The spacer buys nothing and adds a node `paintRail()` must emit.
5. It breaks small phones. A fixed 24px gap is inelastic where `space-around` was elastic. At 320px CSS width the capsule's inner edge is 311 and the fixed rule puts the avatar's right edge at 313.5 — 2.5px of clip, with the add tile jammed at 273. Current build at 320 ends at 303, comfortably inside. Measured at 320 / 360 / 375 / 390.

refuted.why:
REFUTED. The two anchor measurements are frame-accurate — I pixel-scanned both shipped PNGs (`shots/paper-timeline.owner-flight--390x844.png`, `--768x1024.png`) and confirmed the origin ink at 632–640 CSS (box top 629) at 390 and 749–756 (box top 745) at 768, so the seat's 629/745 are right and the first `.b-copy` does land at 853/1033. Everything the finding builds on top of those two numbers is wrong.

1. WRONG EDGE. The finding blames the fold and reads meaning into "the identical 9px at two unrelated widths". The fold is not what cuts. The scroller is `main.app.sheet[data-app="timeline"]`, and the same pixel scan puts its bottom at **765.5** at 390 and **1011.5** at 768 (driven live: 766 / 1012). At 390 the first moment is **87px below the sheet's edge and 78px above the fold** — the 9px coincidence is an artefact of two numbers that never meet. Buying back the 9px the finding reasons from would reveal nothing at either width.

2. THREE DERIVED NUMBERS ARE WRONG. Bare rule below the origin is **121px** at 390 (not 215) and **250px** at 768 (not 279), because both were measured to the fold rather than to the sheet edge. "~230px the first moment needs" is wrong at both: to fully reveal the copy you need **178px** at 390 and **100px** at 768.

3. "NOTHING ON THE FIRST SCREEN SAYS SO" IS FALSE, in the finding's own frames. `.b-gapNote` — "Nothing is planned until 1 August." — sits at 503–515 CSS at 390 and 633–645 at 768, well above the cut, and says in a sentence exactly what the empty run means. And the run is not untuned emptiness: origin→first copy is **224px at `data-px=14`** (390) and **288px at `data-px=18`** (768), i.e. exactly 16 days × pixels-per-day. In Direction B the emptiness is the organising object; the finding reads locked geometry as a layout accident to be reclaimed.

4. FIX (a) CANNOT WORK, AND IS UNAVAILABLE AT 390. The count has exactly two ramp steps in the entire product: `--size-count` (96px, phone) and `--size-countWide` (148px, sheet/desk). At 390 `.b-num` is **already at 96px** — the ramp floor — so "step down one ramp step" means inventing a third step under a gate that asserts the ramp. At 768, 148→96 saves 47px of line box and closing the `.b-gapNote`/`.b-measureBar` band (650→678) buys ~20 more: **~67px against 100px needed**. More fundamentally, the fix is structurally void: the origin-to-moment distance is locked, so every pixel lifted off the hero lifts the origin *and* the moment by the same amount — you must delete 178px from everything above the measure at 390 to move the moment one screen's worth. It also unpicks a recorded earlier fix: `--track-display-148` is bound to the 148px step by the comment at timeline.css:1777.

5. FIX (b) IS BUILT ON A FALSE PREMISE AND WOULD BE A SECOND GRAMMAR FOR A ROLE THAT ALREADY HAS ONE. The `data-more-left/right` fades are scoped `[data-app="tasks"] .sheet` (tasks.css:196, 206) — the timeline sheet ships neither; I read `::before`/`::after` on it at both widths and both are `content: none`. So "the vertical twin of the horizontal fade it already ships" is wrong twice, because the vertical twin already exists **in timeline**: `markFold()` (timeline.js:1399–1408) writes `data-fold="below|above|both"` from `scrollTop + clientHeight < scrollHeight - 2`, driving a **48px** `mask-image` (timeline.css:1952–1960), under a source comment that states the law — "a permanent gradient would be the always-on decoration the defect library forbids". The finding proposes a **96px ::after gradient on opacity gated at > 4** for the same role: a second size, a second mechanism, a second threshold. That is the "N treatments for one role" class this panel has refuted repeatedly here (three-eyebrows-for-one-role, keycap-three-treatments, eyebrow-drawn-three-ways). The 96px is borrowed from Tasks, where the number is justified by card width ("past ~104 it starts eating a legible card"), a reason that does not transfer to a vertical edge.

6. SEVERITY. Not blocking (the sheet scrolls, one notch brings the moment up — the finding says so), not misleading (the gap sentence is true and present). At most a refinement: the shipped law deliberately reserves the fade for a *pane* that hides something unexpectedly, and at ≤768 the sheet is the page, whose bottom edge is the fold every reader already understands. Linear, Stripe and Vercel do not gradient the bottom of the document on a phone.

Tasks and Notes both render the floating dock at the foot — measured 385x48 at x=568,y=876 on tasks.board and 413x46 at x=555,y=878 on notes.notebook — and both pin the sheet's identity: `.word` holds y=38 through any amount of scrolling, because the scroller is an inner region (`.trayBody` 563/608, `.index` 556/949), not the sheet. Timeline renders no `.dock` at all in owner-flight, desk or phone, at 1440 or at 768, and makes `.app.sheet` itself the scroller (864/1173). Set that scroller to scrollTop 249 and the 'timeline.' wordmark measures y = -191 — off the top of the sheet — taking MARA & FINN, the 79, and TODAY IS 16 JULY with it. COMPOSITION.md line 209 justifies the missing dock with 'Timeline has no dock and no add verb', but Timeline's page head carries Add a moment, so the stated premise is false.
unadjudicated.consequence: Crossing the spine from Tasks into Timeline, the foot of the application empties and the app's own name scrolls off the top. Those two objects are the entire visual argument that this is one product; Timeline has neither, so a person who has been working in Tasks reads Timeline as a different application that borrowed the rail. It is the single place a discerning stranger would stop believing one studio made this.
unadjudicated.fix: Mount the dock on Timeline with the verbs it already has — Add a moment, the account tile — plus a search field carrying the same honest-door sentence Tasks' dock field uses. Move Timeline's scroll boundary off `.app.sheet` onto the region below the head block (the measure plus BEHIND YOU), so the wordmark and the distance head are outside the scroller exactly as Tasks' and Notes' heads are.
unadjudicated.assertion: At 1440x960 and 768x1024, in every one of the eight states, a `.dock` renders with width > 200. And in every state, after setting that product's scroller to scrollTop 300, the bounding-box y of the visible `.word` equals its value at scrollTop 0.

unadjudicated.element: Timeline — `[data-layout-to]` on the measure's head, and the `.b-undo` strip
unadjudicated.problem: Driven at 1440x960 on ?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight, both runs identical except for one extra press. Run A: open Menu tasting via `.b-grab`, press 'Move a week later', press Done. The strip reads 'Menu tasting at The Orchard moved 7 days later. Undo Ctrl Z' (1130x54) and Ctrl+Z restores Sat 1 Aug. Run B: same, then press ACROSS to DOWN. The strip collapses to 0x0 and its sentence is gone; Ctrl+Z now changes nothing — the moment stays at Sat 8 Aug — and no live region changes. Timeline also has no fallback: pressing Ctrl+Z on a rested Timeline announces nothing, where Tasks announces 'Nothing left to undo.'
unadjudicated.consequence: Orla moves a wedding milestone by a week, changes how she is looking at the measure, presses the undo key the product taught her in Tasks, and the surface does nothing and says nothing. She cannot tell whether the undo failed, whether the move ever happened, or whether she pressed the wrong key — on the one screen whose entire job is telling her how far off a date is. A reversal that is silently withdrawn and then answered with silence is worse than never offering one.
unadjudicated.fix: Carry the pending undo record across the orientation re-render — the layout switch rebuilds the measure and must not reset the record — and keep the strip's sentence with it. Separately, when Ctrl+Z is pressed on Timeline with no record, announce Tasks' sentence 'Nothing left to undo.' through Timeline's `.sr` region.
unadjudicated.assertion: Move a moment, press Done, switch orientation, press Ctrl+Z: the moment returns to its original date and a live region announces the reversal. And on a rested Timeline in both orientations, Ctrl+Z announces 'Nothing left to undo.'

unadjudicated.element: Notes — the seam's Ctrl+Z
unadjudicated.problem: Driven at 1440x960 on ?v=paper&state=notes.seam. Pressing `[data-act="send"]` moves focus to `.deskFactLink` ('Open in Tasks: Switch on before guests arrive, not when'). Pressing Ctrl+Z announces 'Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks.' and leaves `document.activeElement === document.body`. The same key driven on tasks.board in the same session returns focus to the exact `.tick` it started on ('Mark done') and announces the card by name. r1 closed `undo-drops-focus-on-body` and `undo-drops-focus-to-body`; the Tasks path is fixed and the Notes seam path measured today is not — I am reporting the seam path as still open, not re-raising the Tasks one.
unadjudicated.consequence: The keyboard user reverses the product's signature gesture and is dropped at the top of the document; their next Tab restarts the whole surface. Undo is the gesture that makes a person brave enough to try the seam at all, and here it is the gesture that costs them their place.
unadjudicated.fix: On the seam's undo, restore focus to the control that opened it — `[data-act="send"]` on the peeled sheet if still mounted, otherwise the note body the words were peeled from — the same restore the Tasks tick path already performs.
unadjudicated.assertion: On notes.seam at 1440x960 and 390x844: press Send, then Ctrl+Z; `document.activeElement` is inside `.desk` and is not `document.body`.

unadjudicated.element: Tasks — `.trayBody` bottom edge, state tasks.dense
unadjudicated.problem: At 1920x1000 on ?v=paper&state=tasks.dense, `.trayBody` clips at clientHeight 663 against scrollHeight 1081. The shipped edge treatment is `.tray::after`: a 1px rule at bottom:39px with `background-image: none` — a hairline, not a fade. The clip lands mid-glyph: 'ENQUIRY' in To do and 'Aisling & Tom' in In progress are both sliced horizontally through the middle of their letterforms, with the hairline drawn across the cut. This is not the r1 finding `tray-clips-cards-mid-line`, which claimed no edge treatment ships and was refuted on that measurement; the treatment ships, and this is what it produces at the declared width.
unadjudicated.consequence: At the density the customer actually runs — 32 tasks, the state literally named dense — two of five columns end in a word sawn in half with a line drawn through it, and the 'Add here' row underneath reads as part of the severed card. A stranger reads that as a broken render, not as 'there is more below'. It is the one frame in the set that would fail the 'a top studio made this' test on sight.
unadjudicated.fix: Replace the hairline with a bottom mask on `.trayBody` that fades the last 28px to transparent whenever scrollHeight exceeds clientHeight, and add one line-height of bottom padding inside the scroller so the clip line never lands inside a glyph body.
unadjudicated.assertion: At every declared viewport, for every `.trayBody` where scrollHeight > clientHeight, computed `mask-image` (or `-webkit-mask-image`) is not 'none'; and at 1920x1000 on tasks.dense no text element's box is bisected by the clip line — every clipped element's top sits at least one line-height above it or entirely below it.

unadjudicated.element: Ctrl/Cmd+K and the dock search field, across the three products
unadjudicated.problem: Driven at 1440x960. Ctrl+K on notes.notebook opens `.searchTop`, focuses the input and announces 'Search everything you wrote.' Ctrl+K on tasks.board announces the honest door 'Search arrives with the other views.' Ctrl+K on timeline.owner-flight does nothing: no overlay, no focus change, and no live region content at all. Separately, Tasks' `.dockField` carries `aria-label="Search comes with the other views."` while the key announces 'Search arrives with the other views.' — one door, two sentences.
unadjudicated.consequence: The person learns a key in Notes, carries it into Timeline, and gets silence — the exact answer the honest-doors system was designed to prevent, delivered on the one product where the door is not even drawn. And a screen-reader user on Tasks hears the same closed door described two different ways inside one gesture, which makes the honesty read as sloppiness.
unadjudicated.fix: Bind Ctrl/Cmd+K once in the suite shell rather than per product, so Timeline answers it through `.sr` with its own honest-door sentence in the established grammar ('Search arrives with the other views.'). Make Tasks' dock field `aria-label` and the announced sentence one shared string constant.
unadjudicated.assertion: Pressing Ctrl+K in each of the eight states changes at least one live region's text; and Tasks' `.dockField` `aria-label` is byte-identical to the sentence the key announces.

unadjudicated.element: The nine `aria-disabled="true"` doors, rail and dock
unadjudicated.problem: Measured at 1440x960 and 390x844 across all three products. All five rail doors (mark, home, inbox, help, me) and Notes' `.dockAvatar` compute `cursor: pointer` while carrying `aria-disabled="true"`; Tasks' `.dockField` and Tasks' `.dockAvatar` compute `cursor: default`. The accessible names disagree too: Notes' dock tile is `aria-label="Orla, venue manager. Not here yet."` while Tasks' dock tile and both rail avatars are `aria-label="Orla, venue manager"` with the sentence only in `title`. r1's `two-account-tiles-one-honest` was closed by putting the sentence into one of the three account tiles, which is what created the split.
unadjudicated.consequence: A mouse user gets a hand cursor over seven doors that will not open. A screen-reader user hears the same account door named two different ways depending which product they happen to be standing in. The honest-doors idea is the most distinctive decision on this surface; applying it inconsistently is what makes it read as an unfinished feature rather than a stance.
unadjudicated.fix: One rule in the shell: every element with `aria-disabled="true"` takes `cursor: default`, and its accessible name is composed as `<name>. <the not-here-yet sentence>` from the same string that fills `title`. Delete the per-product variants.
unadjudicated.assertion: In every state at 1440x960 and 390x844, every `[aria-disabled="true"]` has computed `cursor` other than 'pointer', and its `aria-label` ends with the exact sentence its `title` carries.

unadjudicated.element: Notes — the send confirmation
unadjudicated.problem: On notes.seam at 1440x960, pressing `[data-act="send"]` changes two `role="status"` regions in the same frame: `.undo` (317x46) to 'Sent to Tasks. Undo Ctrl Z for 30 seconds' and `.sr` (1x1) to 'Sent to Tasks. Your note stayed here. In The house.' Tasks' tick, driven in the same session, changes only `.sr`. The seam is the only gesture in the suite that changes two live regions at once.
unadjudicated.consequence: On the one gesture the whole suite exists to justify, a screen-reader user hears 'Sent to Tasks' twice, in two different sentences, one of which runs a countdown. The confirmation that should feel like relief arrives as a stutter.
unadjudicated.fix: Mark the visible undo strip `aria-hidden="true"` and let `.sr` carry the whole confirmation including the reversal offer and its window, the way the Tasks tick path already does.
unadjudicated.assertion: On notes.seam, pressing Send changes the text of exactly one element matching `[aria-live], [role="status"]`.

unadjudicated.element: Timeline · .b-gapNote (src/timeline.js:403 gapSentence, :869 the empty branch)
unadjudicated.problem: The sentence directly under the countdown reads "Nothing is planned until 1 August." It asserts emptiness with no noun. Driven at 1440 and 1920, across and down, on timeline.owner-flight, timeline.desk and timeline.phone: the string is identical in all twelve. Two clicks away on the spine, Tasks shows "Build the Saturday run-sheet — Due today — Mara & Finn. High priority" and "Order tonic and the good olives — 2 days overdue", and the head chips read "1 today" and "1 overdue". Scoping to the couple does not rescue it: the due-today task is Mara & Finn's. As three separate products the sentence was true of each product's own objects. As one application it is a false statement about the world the person is looking at. The empty-state twin, "Nothing is planned yet.", has the same shape.
unadjudicated.consequence: Orla opens the plan for the wedding she is running and reads that her next fortnight is clear. It is not: something is due today and something is two days overdue, both hers, both for this couple. The one sentence on the sheet that she can act on without reading anything else is the one that will send her away from her desk.
unadjudicated.fix: In src/timeline.js, change gapSentence() to return "The next moment is " + F.fmt.medium(nearestIso) + "." and the empty branch in writeGap() to "No moments on this plan yet." Positive, declarative, and it names the object class the same screen already uses three times ("Add a moment", "3 moments", "Delete this moment").
unadjudicated.assertion: Across all three Timeline states × layout=across|down × 390/768/1280/1440/1920, no rendered .b-gapNote contains the substring "Nothing is planned", and every rendered .b-gapNote contains "moment" or "moments".

unadjudicated.element: Notes · .peelBoundary in notes.seam — "Your note stays here. Tasks only ever receives the exact words you pick and check below."
unadjudicated.problem: Driven at 1440 on ?state=notes.seam: I replaced the whole of .peelField with "Completely different words Orla typed" — a string that appears nowhere in the note — pressed Send to Tasks, walked the spine to Tasks, and read the card title: "Completely different words Orla typed". What crosses is the contents of the field, not the words picked. Even untouched the claim is not exact: the picked run is "Switch on before guests arrive, not when." and the field is seeded "Switch on before guests arrive, not when" — the terminal stop is dropped. The clause "and check below" is doing all the work and is doing it invisibly: fifteen words, a compound relative, and a dangling "below". This is the sentence the entire argument for a suite rests on, printed in the state named after the seam.
unadjudicated.consequence: Orla reads the field as a preview of a guarantee rather than as the editor it is, so she leaves the wording alone — and the card that lands on the board is the sentence fragment "Switch on before guests arrive, not when", which is a poor task and reads as one. The product's central trust claim is the one sentence on the surface that does not survive being tested.
unadjudicated.fix: Replace .peelBoundary with two short declaratives that are true under every reading and point at the control: "Your note stays here. Tasks gets only the words in the box below." Drop "only ever", "exact" and "pick" — the box is the guarantee, so name the box.
unadjudicated.assertion: The rendered .peelBoundary matches /Tasks gets only the words in the box below/ and contains neither "pick" nor "exact"; and a driven test that fills .peelField with a string absent from .readBody, presses [data-act=send] and reads the new .cardTitle in Tasks passes without contradicting any sentence on screen.

unadjudicated.element: Notes · .idxWhen on crossed .idxRow in notes.seam, against Tasks · .when in the Done tray
unadjudicated.problem: The r1 finding ledger-time-reads-as-completion was fixed in the accessible name only. Driven and read at 1440: the row's aria-label now correctly says "Send registrar paperwork two weeks before the date. In Tasks, Done. Sent to Tasks 2 days ago. The note it came from stayed in Notes." The visible row still reads "Send registrar paperwork two weeks before the date · Done · 2 days ago", with the time abutting a pill that says Done and no word between them. On the Tasks board the same task carries "2 Jul" and the name "Completed 2 Jul". Today is 16 July. One application prints two dates fourteen days apart for one task. Same pattern on "Clear Sunday 11am late checkout" — Notes "20 hours ago", Tasks "14 Jul". I am raising this as the suite fact, which no standalone Notes round could see, not as the closed r1 finding; the sighted string is unchanged and I measured it.
unadjudicated.consequence: The seam ledger is where Orla checks that the handoff worked. Read on its own it says three things were finished in the last two days. Cross-checked against Tasks it is off by up to two weeks on every row, and the one surface whose whole job is to prove the seam is trustworthy is the one that does not agree with the board.
unadjudicated.fix: In notes.js, render the crossed row's visible time with the verb its accessible name already uses: .idxWhen prints "Sent 2 days ago" rather than "2 days ago". One word, and the visible string then carries the same fact as the name.
unadjudicated.assertion: For every crossed .idxRow, the rendered text of .idxWhen begins with "Sent " and the remainder is character-identical to the interval named in that row's aria-label after "Sent to Tasks ".

unadjudicated.element: Tasks · .carryName inside .carry, at 390×844 after a tick
unadjudicated.problem: Measured in Chromium at 390×844 with touch, after ticking the first card: .carryName holds "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company done" at scrollWidth 289 against clientWidth 246, text-overflow: ellipsis. The strip renders "Confirm marquee sides with the hire comp… Undo". The 43px that gets cut is the word "done" — the only word in the strip that says what happened — plus the tail of "company", cut at the character, which is the mid-word clamp class the defect library already paid for once. At 768 and above the full string survives. The strip is also the phone's only route to undo, and it is on screen for six seconds (measured).
unadjudicated.consequence: On the device the fixture itself says Orla works from — "something that works on a phone out at the marquee" — the reversibility strip names an object and an action button and never says what it will reverse. Completed, moved and deleted all produce a strip that reads the same way. She has six seconds to decide whether to press a button whose sentence has had its verb removed.
unadjudicated.fix: Move the verb out of .carryName into its own non-shrinking element rendered first, so the strip reads "Done · Confirm marquee sides with the hire company" and the ellipsis falls on the title, and trim that title to the last whole word rather than letting text-overflow: ellipsis cut at the character.
unadjudicated.assertion: At 390×844 with touch, after a tick, the rendered .carry contains the word "done" (or "Done") with no ellipsis between it and the strip's edge, and no text node inside .carry ends part-way through a word.

unadjudicated.element: Timeline · .b-behindState and both .b-behindNote variants (src/timeline.js:1019-1030, :1107-1114)
unadjudicated.problem: One cancelled moment, the city hotel shortlist, is described in four different sentences depending on who is looking and whether a disclosure is open. Driven and read on timeline.owner-flight and timeline.desk at 1440: the row says "Not going ahead"; folded, the owner reads "2 done, the last of them 18 April. One thing is not going ahead."; folded, the guest reads "The Orchard reserved, 18 April. The city hotel shortlist is not going ahead."; opened, either reader gets "One of them did not happen." — a different tense, sitting twenty pixels below a row that says the opposite tense. Two further problems ride on it: the owner's own view is the vaguest of the four, calling a moment "one thing" on a sheet whose count says "3 moments", and opening a disclosure silently rewrites a sentence that was not about the disclosure.
unadjudicated.consequence: Orla's own view of her past tells her less than the version she sends the couple, and the sentence changes tense when she opens the list — so the surface whose entire subject is what has already happened cannot settle on whether it happened or is not going to. Nothing here is wrong; it just never reads like one product wrote it.
unadjudicated.fix: Write one sentence and use it in all four places, present tense, naming the moment: "The city hotel shortlist is not going ahead." Give the owner the same naming sentence the guest gets (drop the count-only branch at :1022), and delete the "One of them did not happen." branch at :1110 rather than swapping sentences on disclosure.
unadjudicated.assertion: Across timeline.owner-flight, timeline.desk and timeline.phone, folded and open: every rendered .b-behindNote that refers to a cancelled moment names that moment by title and contains "is not going ahead"; no rendered string anywhere on the Timeline contains "did not happen"; and the owner's folded note is character-identical to the guest's.

unadjudicated.element: Notes · .darkNote in notes.voice
unadjudicated.problem: "Your browser may send microphone audio to its speech service to turn it into text. Signal Studio does not receive or retain that audio. Your browser or speech provider controls its service retention. Typing stays on your device until you save." Sentence three is compliance boilerplate in a product that writes plain English everywhere else — "its service retention" is a noun stack and "its" has two candidate antecedents. Sentence four changes subject to typing, inside an overlay whose subject is speaking, and so closes a privacy statement on the wrong topic. Four sentences where three would do, in the one paragraph on the surface that has to be believed on first reading.
unadjudicated.consequence: The moment a person is being recorded is the moment the voice has to be at its plainest. This is the only paragraph in the suite that has to be re-read to be understood, and it is the one where re-reading costs trust rather than comprehension.
unadjudicated.fix: Three sentences, same facts, same register as the rest of the product: "Your browser may send what you say to its own speech service to turn it into text. Signal Studio never receives or keeps that audio. How long your browser or its provider keeps it is their decision, not ours." Drop the typing sentence — it belongs on the writing surface, not here.
unadjudicated.assertion: The rendered .darkNote contains exactly three sentences, contains neither "service retention" nor the word "Typing", and every sentence has one unambiguous subject.

unadjudicated.element: Notes · aria-label on .idxRow (src/notes.js:1943-1945)
unadjudicated.problem: The name is built as `${title} ${rest}`.trim() + `. ${src.label}. ${when}.` — but every note body already ends in a full stop, so all fourteen index rows carry a doubled one: "…the florist has to come back twice.. Spoken. 3 hours ago. Still to decide." Measured across all eight states (Notes stays mounted under Tasks and Timeline, so it is 14 malformed strings and 98 sightings, not 14). The crossed rows in notes.seam are clean, which is what shows the join, not the content, is at fault.
unadjudicated.consequence: Every row of the product's primary list hands a screen-reader user a stumble the sighted reader never sees. It costs a beat per row and it is the studio's punctuation appearing twice in a string the studio wrote.
unadjudicated.fix: At notes.js:1943, strip terminal punctuation from the head before joining: const head = `${note.title} ${note.rest || ""}`.trim().replace(/[.!?]+$/, ""); then build the name from head. Write the regex to the file with an editor, not through a shell.
unadjudicated.assertion: In every state, no aria-label or title attribute anywhere in the document matches /\.\.(?!\.)/ or /[.?!]\s+\./.

unadjudicated.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
unadjudicated.element: every `[aria-disabled="true"]` in the suite — `.rail` tiles (master.html:364), `.segItem` List/Schedule/Calendar, `.viewTools` Filter/Sort/Display, `Share`, `More`, `.dockField`, `.dockAvatar`
unadjudicated.problem: The artefact has no visual language for a closed door, anywhere, and pressing one produces no visible change anywhere. Driven at 1440x960 on `?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, sixteen chrome controls sit on the Tasks sheet and **ten of them are aria-disabled**: Share, More, List, Schedule, Calendar, Filter, Sort, Display, the dock's search field (`.dockField`, 211x38, "Search The Orchard, events") and the dock's account tile. Measured computed styles: every one of them paints `rgba(17,17,17,0.62)` at weight 400 — which is `--ink-3`, the token the system uses for live micro-labels at 5.3:1, i.e. fully-available secondary text. The live control beside them, `Planning`, paints `rgba(17,17,17,0.72)`. A 0.10 alpha step is the entire difference. Inside the view segment it is worse: `Board` is the current view (ink-1 / 600 / white pill) and List, Schedule and Calendar are 0.62/400 — identical to how a live-but-unselected segment item would look, so "not selected" and "not built" are the same picture. In the spine this is a regression of a finding recorded closed at r1 (`closed-doors-are-indistinguishable`, classed misleading). Its own recorded assertion was "the computed color differs from a live `.railTile`'s and cursor is not pointer". I measured both halves at 1440 and at 390-touch: `home` (closed) and `notes` (live, not current) both compute `color: rgba(255,255,255,0.62)`, `background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0)`, `cursor: pointer`, `opacity: 1`, `filter: none`. The rule the r1 finding named as dead — `.rail [aria-disabled="true"] { color: var(--on-ink-2) }` at master.html:364 — is still in the file, still setting the colour `.railTile` already has at line 321. The third clause fails too: I snapshotted every element's box, opacity, background and transform before and after a real mouse click on `home`, and exactly one node in the document changed — `P.sr` at 1x1 px, off-screen. Same result for Share, Filter, Sort, Display, List, Schedule and Calendar: each writes its sentence into `#say` and nothing else moves. At 390 with a real touch tap there is no cursor and no tooltip, so the entire signal is zero.
unadjudicated.consequence: On the surface Orla runs her season from, ten of the sixteen controls do nothing and nothing on screen says which. The two she reaches for first are among them: Share — on a board whose own card reads "Share with the floor team" — and the search field, which is the largest, most inviting object in the floating dock, sitting beside a live black Add task button. She presses it, the screen does not move, and she cannot tell whether the app is broken, her tap missed, or the feature is absent. On her phone at the marquee that is the only reading available to her. The locked answer was "present, reachable, and say plainly that they are not here yet"; as shipped, the plainness reaches a screen-reader user and nobody else.
unadjudicated.fix: One token pair and one function call. (1) Give closed a real ink step: add `cursor: default` to `.rail [aria-disabled="true"]` and replace the dead rule at master.html:364 with `color: var(--on-ink-3)` (rgba(255,255,255,0.42), already declared); on the white sheet, move every `[aria-disabled="true"]` control from `--ink-3` to `--ink-4` and lift the live secondary controls (`Planning`, `.segItem` not current) to `--ink-2`, so the density step separates closed from live rather than current from not-current. This is ink density only — no new colour, no new weight. Disabled controls are exempt from WCAG 1.4.3, so the contrast pass should exclude `[aria-disabled="true"]` rather than block this. (2) Make the press visible: the suite already renders a bottom-centre strip for undo (`undoStrip()`, master.html:12747). Route the sentence the door already carries into that same strip for one beat when any `[aria-disabled="true"]` control is activated — the rail click interceptor and the sheet's handlers already have the string in hand and already call `say()`.
unadjudicated.assertion: For every `[aria-disabled="true"]` element in every state at 390, 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920, its computed `color` differs from that of a live sibling control in the same group and its computed `cursor` is not `pointer`; and after activating it by real pointer click, by Enter, and by real touch tap at 390, the sentence it carries is present in a node whose bounding rect is larger than 1x1 for at least one frame.

unadjudicated.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
unadjudicated.element: the card the seam produces on the Tasks board — `.card[data-id^="seam_"] .cardTitle` and `.cardNote`
unadjudicated.problem:
Drove the seam end to end at 1440 on `?state=notes.seam`: selected words, `[data-act="peel"]`, `[data-act="send"]`, then Enter on "Open in Tasks". The card that lands in To do renders its own title twice. `

Switch on before guests arrive, not when

` is followed by `

Switch on before guests arrive, not when.

` — the same string, differing only by a full stop. The screen-reader path repeats it too: `aria-label="Switch on before guests arrive, not when"` with `aria-describedby` pointing at `Switch on before guests arrive, not when. The house.`, so the name is read and then immediately read again. Every other card on the board either carries a body that says something the title does not ("Mara & Finn, Saturday. Terrace plan if dry, marquee if not…") or carries no body at all ("Reprint the faded welcome sign before the open day"), so a body-less card is already a supported shape in this system.
unadjudicated.consequence: The seam is the whole argument for a suite existing, and its output object stutters. Orla peels a line, sends it, is taken to Tasks, and the first thing she sees on the card she just made is her own sentence written out twice — the one card on the board that reads like a bug. Worse, the peel has thrown away the context that made the line legible: three weeks later "Switch on before guests arrive, not when" says nothing about heating, the orchard room, or October, and the card's body — the one place that context belonged — is spent restating the title.
unadjudicated.fix: Do not populate `cardNote` from the peeled string. Set it to the note's remaining sentences, trimmed to the card's two-line clamp — for the shipped fixture, "Heating: orchard room takes ~40 min to warm in October. Note for the winter brochure couples." — which is the material the peel removed and the only text that makes the task readable later. When the peeled words are the whole note, omit `cardNote` entirely and render the body-less card shape that already ships. In the same pass, drop the title from the `cd-` description span and leave it carrying the project alone ("The house."), so the accessible name is not spoken twice.
unadjudicated.assertion: After driving Notes → peel → send → open-task, the landed card's `.cardTitle` textContent and its `.cardNote` textContent are not equal once trailing punctuation and whitespace are normalised (or `.cardNote` is absent); and the card's accessible description does not start with its accessible name.

unadjudicated.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard

unadjudicated.element: Notes · [data-act="undo"] after a seam send
unadjudicated.problem: After sending words to Tasks from `notes.seam`, all three routes to taking it back leave `document.activeElement === document.body`: Ctrl+Z, a click on the visible "Undo" button, and Enter on that button. I drove all three at 1440×960 and got BODY every time, while the live region correctly reads "Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks." and the peel panel is correctly restored with `.peelField` back at y 400. The equivalent path in Tasks does this right — undoing a tick restores focus to the card's own `.tick` — so the two halves of one suite disagree about what undo owes the keyboard.
unadjudicated.consequence: A keyboard or screen-reader user takes back a send and is dropped out of the document into nowhere: the AT's cursor resets, nothing is spoken about where she now is, and she has to rebuild her position by feel even though the panel she was working in is sitting restored on screen in front of her.
unadjudicated.fix: Give the seam's undo the same `refocus` record the peel's other transitions already use — `refocus = { kind: "field", sel: ".peelField", end: true }`, which is exactly what `[data-act="peel"]` sets at src/notes.js:1042 — so the restored wording field takes focus after the repaint, on all three routes.
unadjudicated.assertion: From `?state=notes.seam` at 1440×960 and at 390×844, press `[data-act="send"]`, then undo by each of Ctrl+Z, clicking `[data-act="undo"]`, and Enter on `[data-act="undo"]`; assert in every case that `document.activeElement !== document.body` and that it is inside `.peel`.

unadjudicated.element: Notes · the "Already in Tasks" ledger (`src/notes.js:2434-2436`, `idxRow(..., {mode:"crossed"})` at :1928-1965) and the notebook corpus (`work()` at :205, `N.notes` vs `N.crossed` in `src/fixture.js:562-563`)
unadjudicated.problem: The seam's central promise is asserted in three places and is false for every note the fixture says has already crossed. The strapline reads "3 so far, and every note stayed here"; each row's accessible name ends "The note it came from stayed in Notes."; the seam card says "Your note stays here" and the receipt says "still yours to edit". Driven at 1440: the three crossed notes (s1 late-checkout, s2 linen, s3 registrar) are in NO index — `notes.notebook` lists 14 `.idxRow`s and none of them is one of the three; they are not in the search corpus — `Ctrl+K` "linen" announces "No note says “linen”. Nothing in the notebook is close to it either." while `fixture.js:486` holds a note body reading "Linen supplier rang, the order now ships Tuesday…", and "supplier" returns "1 of 14 notes", matching the photographer note and not that one; and `/Linen supplier rang/.test(document.body.innerText)` is false at every state. The cause is structural: `work()` returns `N.notes.slice()` and `N.crossed` is a disjoint array that is rendered only as task wording. Each ledger row is a real `<button class="idxRow" tabindex=0>` with a full accessible name, and pressing any of the three (nth 0, 1, 2) produces no announcement, no state change and no note — a focusable, named control that does nothing. A note sent live in-session behaves correctly (send "Heating" → still among the 14, still searchable, index row gains an "In Tasks" pill), which proves the intended behaviour exists and that only the pre-crossed notes are stranded.
unadjudicated.consequence: Orla is told, in the accessible name of every row and in the sentence above them, that the note she sent is still hers. She presses the row to get back to it and nothing happens; she searches the word she wrote and the product tells her flatly that she never wrote it. This is the one claim the whole suite exists to make, and on the three examples the product chooses to show her, the claim is untrue and the way back is a dead button.
unadjudicated.fix: Put `N.crossed` into the notebook corpus: in `src/notes.js:205`, return `N.notes.concat(N.crossed)` (sorted by `ago`) so the three crossed notes are ordinary index rows carrying the existing "In Tasks" pill and are inside the `matchWindow()` search corpus. Leave the ledger's rendering exactly as it is — the comment at :1930-1934 is right that the ledger must not reprint the private note — but wire its row's press to the handler an ordinary `.idxRow` already uses (`data-id` → lift that note onto the desk), so "The note it came from stayed in Notes" has somewhere to go. The head count moves from 14 to 17, which is the honest number.
unadjudicated.assertion: At `?state=notes.notebook`, `Ctrl+K` + "linen" announces a match (not "No note says"), and `document.querySelectorAll('.idxRow[data-id="s2"]')` exists in the "Your notes" index; at `?state=notes.seam`, pressing the "Already in Tasks" row for s2 puts "Linen supplier rang" into `document.body.innerText`.

unadjudicated.element: Timeline · `p.b-live` (`src/timeline.js:2246, 2307, 2662, 2890`) written by `go()` at :2179-2184, by "Add a moment" at :2432-2433, and by the copy/publish receipts at :1979 and :2672
unadjudicated.problem: `go(state)` calls `C.mount()` — a full repaint that destroys the `.b-live` node — and then does `document.querySelector(".b-live").textContent = SAID[state]` on the freshly created replacement. A region inserted into the document already containing its text is not a mutation of a region assistive technology was watching, so none of it is ever announced. Measured directly: I marked the live nodes at load and watched `document.body` for subtree changes. Pressing Preview logs `REMOVED a .b-live` then `ADDED a .b-live with text: "The plan as guests will see it."` and fires zero mutations on any watched region; pressing "Get the link" logs `ADDED a .b-live with text: "Ready to copy."`, again zero. A second run confirms node identity: `.b-live` goes ny9fux → n80t9e → npgkp9 across three acts while the suite's `p.sr` stays `nk8cdg` throughout. The same acts change the whole surface — Preview replaces the three-button bar with one "Back to the plan" and takes `.b-grab` from 7 to 0, removing every edit control — and Escape does nothing. Tasks and Notes are clean by contrast (`p.sr` alive and mutating on tick, filter, Planning, send). The file knows: the orientation switch at :2959-2969 was moved to `window.__SUITE.say()` with a comment explaining exactly this, and the comment above `go()` at :2166-2169 claims the cure — "three of the owner's five top-level actions were silent screen changes" — while the mechanism leaves them silent.
unadjudicated.consequence: A screen-reader user presses Preview and every Edit affordance on the plan disappears with nothing said. The same for Back to the plan, Add a moment and Get the link. Four of Timeline's top-level actions are unspoken screen changes, and the loss of seven edit controls with no announcement reads as data loss rather than a mode change.
unadjudicated.fix: In `src/timeline.js`, replace every `document.querySelector(".b-live").textContent = …` with `window.__SUITE.say(…)`, called after the focus restore, exactly as the orientation switch does at :2968. Four sites: `go()` at :2183-2184, "A moment was added." at :2432-2433, and the two receipts at :1979 and :2672. Keep `p.b-live` as the visible receipt, but drop `role="status"` from it so one act cannot be queued twice.
unadjudicated.assertion: Attach a MutationObserver to the live-region node that exists BEFORE the press; pressing Preview, Back to the plan, Add a moment and Get the link each fires a text mutation on a node that is still `document.contains(...)` afterwards — i.e. the identity of the announcing region is unchanged across the act.

unadjudicated.element: `src/shell.css:216-219` — `.rail button:focus-visible, .rail [tabindex]:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--indigo); outline-offset: 2px }`
unadjudicated.problem: The spine's keyboard focus ring is indigo #4f46e5 drawn at 2px offset onto the rail's ink surface. Measured from real pixels (screenshot the focused tile, count colours): the ring paints rgb(79,70,229) on a surround of rgb(33,33,33) — **2.56:1**, below the 3:1 floor WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 sets for focus indicators. Reproduced on `.railTile[data-rail="notes"]` and `.railAvatar` at 1440 in tasks.board and at 390 in timeline.phone (identical 234-pixel ring, identical 2.56:1), and on `.railMark` and the current tile, whose rings also land on rgb(33,33,33) rather than on the tile beneath them. The spine is the first tab stop in all three products, so this is the first focus indication a keyboard user ever gets. The product already solves it correctly elsewhere and only ever on the ink ground: `src/notes.css:954` sets `.dark :focus-visible { outline-color: var(--white) }` for the dictation overlay and `:1623` sets the same for the phone dock — measured at 18.88:1 on `.dockGlyph`. The rule's own comment says "The spine's focus ring is the spine's, not the mounted product's" — it unified the ring and kept the sheet's colour for a ground that is not the sheet. The audit cannot see this: `outlineColor` appears only in the palette membership list (`gates/*-audit.mjs`), and indigo is a legal palette colour, so non-text contrast is ungated.
unadjudicated.consequence: A keyboard user's only indication of where they are in the suite's primary navigation is a ring at 2.56:1 on black — visible on a good monitor, effectively gone in daylight, on a laptop panel, or for anyone with reduced contrast sensitivity. It is a bare WCAG AA failure on the object every product shares, at every width, and the founder currently believes AA is guarded.
unadjudicated.fix: In `src/shell.css:216-219`, change `outline: 2px solid var(--indigo)` to `outline: 2px solid var(--white)`, keeping `outline-offset: 2px`. White on rgb(33,33,33) measures 12.6:1, and the 2px offset keeps a dark gap between the ring and the white current-page tile so the ring still reads as a ring. This is the same decision `notes.css:954` and `:1623` already made, applied to the one ink-ground object that was missed; it introduces no colour.
unadjudicated.assertion: Focus each `.rail` tile, `.railAvatar`, `.railAdd` and `.railMark` at 390 and 1440 in all three products, screenshot the tile plus 8px of surround, and require the ring colour to measure ≥ 3.0:1 against the most common surrounding colour in that crop.

unadjudicated.element: Tasks · `.trayAdd` tabindex expression (`src/tasks.js:651-653`) and the lane walk (`walk()`), against the Waiting lane at `tasks.board`
unadjudicated.problem: This is a re-raise of `waiting-lane-is-keyboard-inert` (r1, CONFIRMED, recorded closed). I re-ran that finding's own recorded assertion and it fails exactly as written. Measured at 1440: `.trayAdd` tabindex map is `To do:0, In progress:-1, Review:-1, Waiting:-1, Done:-1`; a 120-press Tab sweep at each of 390, 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920 never reaches "Add a task to Waiting" (14 stops at 390, 17 at every other width, the only Add row visited being "Add a task to To do"); and a breadth-first search over ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown from the roving card, to depth 6, reaches all 13 cards and **zero** `.trayAdd` buttons. ArrowRight from Review lands on Done, skipping the empty lane entirely; ArrowDown past the last card in a lane stays on that card. The rover-follows-the-card mechanism works — moving the rover into Done flips Done's Add to tabindex 0 — which is precisely why a lane with no cards can never hold it. Confirmed as an emptiness defect and not a Waiting defect: at `tasks.dense`, where Waiting holds 2 cards, the same pattern gives `10/0, 7/-1, 4/-1, 2/-1, 9/-1` and Waiting is reachable. Nothing in `interaction-check.mjs` asserts anything about `.trayAdd`, which is why this was recorded closed without being closed (lessons L-05).
unadjudicated.consequence: The one lane with nothing in it is the one lane a keyboard user cannot put anything into. The empty state says the right thing — "Nothing held up." — and then offers a first move that no key sequence can reach, which is the exact shape the empty-state rule exists to prevent. It also means a founder's ledger currently records a defect as fixed that a keyboard user still hits.
unadjudicated.fix: Extend the rover, not the tab order, in `walk()`: ArrowDown from the last card in a lane moves focus to that lane's `.trayAdd`, and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight into a lane with no rows focuses its `.trayAdd` instead of skipping the lane. Keep all five at `tabindex="-1"` except the one holding the rover, so the roving model at `src/tasks.js:651-653` is unchanged. Track the rover position as `{lane, index|"add"}` rather than `focusId` alone, so an empty lane is a legal position.
unadjudicated.assertion: At `?state=tasks.board`, starting from the roving `.card`, some sequence of ArrowRight/ArrowDown focuses `[aria-label="Add a task to Waiting"]`, and a BFS over the four arrow keys from any card reaches all five `.trayAdd` buttons; repeated at 390 and 1440.

unadjudicated.element: `interaction-check.mjs` — the visibility test at the "nothing invisible can take focus" block and the clipping test at "no silent text clipping"
unadjudicated.problem: The brief states both gates pass. `node interaction-check.mjs` exits 1: "45 assertions, 2 failing" — `FAIL nothing invisible can take focus — button.headNext, button.chip, button.headAct, button.headAct` and `FAIL no silent text clipping (hidden overflow without ellipsis) — span.sr ×6`. Both are the gate's own false positives, verified against the page. `button.headNext` sits inside `div.app[inert]` with `display:none`: `el.closest("[inert]")` is truthy, `el.checkVisibility({checkVisibilityCSS:true,checkOpacity:true})` is `false`, and calling `.focus()` on it leaves `document.activeElement` as BODY — it cannot take focus. The gate reports it because it tests `getComputedStyle(el).display !== "none"` on the element itself, which returns its own `flex` inside a `display:none` ancestor. `span.sr` (25 of them) is the standard visually-hidden pattern — `position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px; overflow:hidden; clip-path:inset(50%)` — with `scrollWidth 830` against `clientWidth 1`, which the clipping rule reads as silent content deletion. Meanwhile the gate's engagement section is still the empty scaffold: it carries the universal floor only, and not one assertion for the keyboard model, undo, the seam or the carry, which is why the r1 `waiting-lane` finding could be recorded closed while still failing.
unadjudicated.consequence: The closing condition for this engagement is "both gates green", and it cannot be evaluated honestly: the gate that would catch a keyboard regression is red for two reasons that have nothing to do with the work, so a real failure would arrive as the third line of an already-failing run and be read as noise. It is also why a confirmed finding was recorded closed without being fixed.
unadjudicated.fix: Two edits in `interaction-check.mjs`. In the focus audit, replace the hand-rolled `visible` test with `const visible = el.checkVisibility({checkVisibilityCSS:true, checkOpacity:true}) && !el.closest("[inert]")`, and skip anything inside `[inert]` before the loop. In the clipping test, skip elements whose `clientWidth <= 1 || clientHeight <= 1` or whose computed `clipPath` is `inset(50%)` — the visually-hidden signature — before the `scrollWidth > clientWidth` comparison. Then prove each rule by breaking what it watches and watching it fail (lessons L-06) before restoring it, and add the four assertions this round's findings carry.
unadjudicated.assertion: `node interaction-check.mjs` exits 0 with zero failures on the unmodified master, AND, with `.sr { position: static; width: auto }` temporarily removed and a real 0-opacity focusable button temporarily added, each of the two rules fires — so neither is passing vacuously.
